title: Stable-window cohort tagging and changelog compiler
creator: Marina Chen
description: Build a deterministic weekly cut process that creates stable 'cohorts' for staggered rollouts across LTS and non-LTS lanes, and an automated changelog compiler that synthesizes PR metadata, semantic labels, and customer-facing release notes. This ticket covers: 1) cohort tagging strategy and fingerprints for RCs, 2) a pre-cut rollout-checker that gates RC creation against smoke tests and telemetry, and 3) a changelog compiler service that assembles structured notes for release notes automation and Console release pages.
acceptance_criteria: Weekly build pipeline produces a cohort tag format: v{MAJOR}.{MINOR}.{PATCH}-cohort{N}-{fingerprint}
RC fingerprint is deterministic and reproducible given commit range + build environment variables
Rollout-checker fails RC creation if smoke tests or core SLO regressions exceed thresholds
Changelog compiler ingests merged PRs across repos and outputs a structured release notes draft in Confluence and a markdown artifact in the release bucket
Console release page shows cohort tag, fingerprint, and rollout schedule automatically
tasks: Design cohort tag schema and backward-compatible mapping for existing LTS lanes
Implement deterministic fingerprinting library in build-tooling (golang)
Add rollout-checker step to weekly CI that queries canary metrics and smoke test results
Implement changelog-compiler microservice that pulls PR metadata and groups by semantic label
Wire changelog output to Confluence template and S3 release artifacts
Add monitoring alerts for failed RC creations and churned cohorts
comments: 2026-03-10 Marina Chen: Created ticket after post-mortem from unstable weekly cut where RC collisions caused client confusion. Drafted cohort/tag idea to reduce rollouts overlapping.

2026-03-11 Liam O'Connor: RFC posted in Confluence (link below). Prefer minimal tag length to avoid downstream parsing changes. Will prototype fingerprint lib in branch: github.com/redwood-inference/release-tooling/pull/142.
2026-03-11 Priya Nair (SRE): Rollout-checker should include a quick KV smoke test and tail 5m error rate from canary dashboards. Noted quota on metrics API may add 30s to CI time.

2026-03-12 Ben Walker (PM): Agreed to conserve current user-visible semver for public endpoints; cohort tags are internal only. PM sign-off for changelog UX: include 'upgrade impact' bullet per release.
2026-03-12 Liam O'Connor: Infra blocker resolved (agent image naming conflict). CI job added: release/cut-cohort with a 10m timeout. Prototype changelog compiled for last two weekly builds attached.
2026-03-12 QA: Found intermittent flakiness in smoke tests when running parallel builds. Temporary mitigation: serialize smoke-run for release pipeline. Follow-up task created.
decisions: Keep public version string unchanged; append cohort metadata as internal tag to avoid breaking customers
Use a SHA256 truncated fingerprint of (commit-range + build-host + docker-image-digest) to ensure reproducible RC identity
Changelog compiler will prioritize PR title and semantic labels (breaking, feature, fix) and fall back to body for description when needed
Rollout-checker thresholds: error-rate delta > 0.5% OR p95 latency increase > 20% OR failing smoke tests => block RC creation
rollout_plan: Week 0: deploy fingerprint library and changelog-compiler to staging; Week 1: enable cohort tagging for non-LTS weekly builds in staging; Week 2: run a dry-run that generates changelog drafts but does not publish; Week 3: enable rollout-checker blocking on staging RCs; Week 4: enable for production weekly pipeline for one cohort (cohort1) then expand to staggered cohorts
notes: Aim is to reduce release churn and make rollouts auditable. Cohort tagging helps evacuate traffic quickly if an RC shows regression by mapping users or tasks to cohorts. Changelog automation should reduce human error in release notes and surface upgrade guidance for customers. Watch for added CI latency from metrics queries—consider caching and rate limiting.
